newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EACA to debate security and ground handling issues.
newsitem.headline: EACA to debate security and ground handling issues.

text.p: Airfreight security and ground handling in the European Community will top the agenda of a meeting of the Netherlands-based European Aircargo Carriers Association (EACA), later this month, chairman Peter Schoute told Reuters.
In a telephone interview, Schoute, the EACA chairman, said the embryonic association will stage its first annual meeting on the Dutch island of Ameland on September 26 and 27.

EACA, which was formed in December 1995 as a new trade association for airline cargo managers, is backed by the Air Cargo Association of the Netherlands, the Air Cargo Managers Association of Belgium and the Airline Operator's Committee Cargo of the United Kingdom.

Schoute said the meeting will be attended by a number of cargo managers representing the interests of groups or existing trade bodies in the Republic of Ireland, Finland, Greece, Austria and Switzerland.
He said: "Our target is to at least acquire three more members, and the countries represented at this meeting will make their decision to join based on the results of the meeting."

Earlier this year, EACA commissioned the Rotterdam-based Erasmus Centre for Logistics and Transport (ECTAL) to circulate a questionnaire to cargo managers throughout Europe, seeking their views on key issues, like security and ground handling, and investigating their views on EACA itself.
Schoute said the questionnaire responses indicated that most managers prefer to discuss the issues on a face-to-face basis.

Initially, ECTAL had planned to publish a study on ground handling in Europe by the end of the summer. Schoute said the views of managers at the EACA AGM will now be incorporated in the study and it will be published later than planned.
